build: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 (version string 0.16.0, the 0.17.0 release branch with ages as merged)

settings.pcalg.ages: pcalg::ages(data) with its defaults: lambda_min = 0.5 log(n), the BIC, adaptive = "none", no degree cap
settings.andrey.ges.numpy.bic: ges with the BIC (ebic_gamma=0.0) and max_parents=9, the first CPDAG of AGES's path

verdict_rule: per setting (strong share, weak share, rows; 20 datasets): D = Andrey - reference per dataset on shd, correct, and wrong; a setting where every dataset has the reference's graph is a tie with every D equal to 0 (same_graph equals paired); otherwise a measure is worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely on its worse side of 0 (above for shd and wrong, below for correct), better when entirely on the other, and the setting is worse if any measure is, better if one is and none is worse, a tie otherwise. mean_D and bootstrap_95 are those of shd. 10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0). A worse setting is rerun on fresh seeds, 20-39, and counts only if it is worse again
error_metric: shd: the variable pairs where the graph differs from every graph between the true CPDAG and the true DAG (a missing or extra edge, an edge directed against the true DAG, or an edge left undirected that the true CPDAG directs, each 1; an edge directed as the true DAG directs it is no error): andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means. precision is the share of a graph's directed edges that the true DAG directs the same way and recall the share of the true DAG's edges the graph directs correctly, the paper's measures, each pooled over the setting's datasets; measures holds the paired comparison of shd, correct (correctly directed edges) and wrong (other directed edges) with the reference, and against_ges the same against Andrey's GES at the same penalty, with the unshielded colliders of the AGES graph that the GES CPDAG lacks
fit_protocol: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, one untimed warm-up fit then one timed fit, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored as a graph; no fit failed or timed out. ratio is the median over the paired datasets of the reference's time over Andrey's
seeds_note: every setting holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19; no setting was worse than the reference, so none was rerun
